flawed_step: Line 0037 (and its propagation through 0040, 0043) in the section "phi|_{S_1 x S_3} is Arbitrary Join Preserving": the proof asserts phi(\bigvee_1 A) = \bigwedge_2 phi[A] "by definition of Frame Homomorphism". Also line 0029 declares A \subseteq S_3, so \bigvee_1 A is not even defined (A must be a subset of S_1).
counterexample: Take L_1 = L_2 = (P({a,b}), \subseteq), which is a frame (joins = unions, finite meets = intersections). Let phi = id, which is a frame homomorphism (it preserves arbitrary joins and finite meets). Then S_3 = phi[S_1] = P({a,b}) and \preceq_3 = \subseteq. Take A = {{a}, {b}} \subseteq S_1. Then \bigvee_1 A = {a} \cup {b} = {a,b}, so LHS = phi(\bigvee_1 A) = {a,b}. But the claimed RHS is \bigwedge_2 phi[A] = {a} \cap {b} = \emptyset. Since {a,b} \ne \emptyset, the asserted identity on line 0037 is false. The same instance refutes line 0040's appeal to Lemma 1 (a statement about suprema \bigvee T \in S_3) to justify an equality between infima \bigwedge_2 and \bigwedge_3.
reasoning_summary: The join-preservation half of the proof is stated with the wrong operation throughout. Lines 0033-0045 begin with phi(\bigvee_1 A) and then equate it to \bigwedge_2 phi[A], \bigwedge_3 phi[A], and \bigwedge_3 (phi|_{S_1 x S_3})[A]. The definition of frame homomorphism recalled at line 0025 gives phi(\bigvee_1 A) = \bigvee_2 phi[A], not a meet; the stated equality is refuted by the identity map on P({a,b}) with A = {{a},{b}}, where the left side is {a,b} and the right side is \emptyset. Line 0048 confirms the mismatch by declaring that \bigvee_1, \bigvee_2, \bigvee_3 are the symbols used in that computation, yet no \bigvee_2 or \bigvee_3 occurs there. The cited justification at line 0041 also misapplies Lemma 1 (closure of S_3 under arbitrary suprema) to a claimed equality of infima; the correct closure fact for infima is Lemma 2, which the proof reserves for the meet section. Additionally, line 0029 takes A \subseteq S_3 rather than A \subseteq S_1, so \bigvee_1 A is undefined for the argument as written (e.g. with L_1 = P({a,b}) and L_2 = the two-element frame, S_3 is not a subset of S_1 in general). Because the displayed chain is the entire content of the join-preservation half, the conclusion that phi|_{S_1 x S_3} is arbitrary join preserving is not established.
